_generic.water: Most plants prefer deep, less frequent watering over daily sprinkling. Water when the top 2-3 cm of soil feels dry, at the base rather than over the leaves. Drooping with wet soil suggests overwatering or root problems; drooping with dry soil suggests underwatering.
_generic.sunlight: Needs vary widely. Many fruit and vegetable crops want 6-8 hours of direct sun; shade-tolerant plants scorch in strong sun. If growth is thin and pale, light may be too low; if leaves bleach or scorch, it may be too strong.
_generic.soil: Most plants need soil that drains well but holds some moisture. Waterlogged soil damages roots; compost improves both drainage and water retention in many soils.
_generic.temp_humidity: Check the preferred range for your species. Sudden swings, frost and heat waves cause stress. High humidity with poor airflow encourages fungal disease.
_generic.nutrients: Pale new growth, purple tints or yellowing between veins can hint at nutrient problems, but similar symptoms come from watering, root or disease issues. Test the soil before fertilising.
_generic.pests: Look for chewed edges or holes, sticky residue, fine webbing, tiny moving insects or eggs on leaf undersides. Start with hand-picking, a water spray or removing affected leaves.

apple.water: Deep water about weekly during dry spells; young trees need more. Avoid wetting foliage in the evening.
apple.sunlight: Full sun, at least 6-8 hours. Prune for open canopies so light and air reach the centre.
apple.soil: Well-drained loam, pH about 6.0-7.0. Avoid sites where water pools.
apple.temp_humidity: Needs winter chill; blossoms are frost sensitive. Wet, humid springs favour scab and other fungal diseases.
apple.nutrients: Do not feed without a soil or leaf test; excess nitrogen gives soft, disease-prone growth.
apple.pests: Watch for aphids, codling moth tunnels in fruit and scale on bark.

blueberry.water: Shallow roots need steady moisture; mulch to keep soil evenly moist but never waterlogged.
blueberry.sunlight: Full sun for best fruiting; tolerates light shade.
blueberry.soil: Acidic, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter, pH about 4.5-5.5. Yellowing between veins on alkaline soil is common.
blueberry.temp_humidity: Cool winters and mild summers suit most varieties.
blueberry.nutrients: Prefers ammonium-type nitrogen sources; check soil pH before adding anything.
blueberry.pests: Birds and spotted-wing fruit flies are the usual problems; netting helps.

cherry.water: Deep, infrequent watering; heavy rain near harvest splits fruit.
cherry.sunlight: Full sun with good air movement.
cherry.soil: Well-drained loam; roots rot quickly in wet soil.
cherry.temp_humidity: Needs winter chill; blossoms are frost sensitive. Humid weather encourages fungal diseases such as powdery mildew.
cherry.nutrients: Feed only if a soil or leaf test shows a need.
cherry.pests: Watch for aphids, cherry fruit fly and birds.

corn.water: About 25 mm (1 inch) per week; do not let it dry out during tasselling and silking.
corn.soil: Fertile, well-drained loam, pH about 5.8-7.0. Plant in blocks rather than single rows for pollination.
corn.temp_humidity: Warm-season crop; seedlings suffer in cold soil. Warm humid weather favours leaf blights and rusts.
corn.nutrients: Heavy nitrogen feeder; pale yellow older leaves starting at the tip can indicate low nitrogen, but confirm with a soil test.
corn.pests: Watch for corn earworm, stem borers, armyworm and aphids.

grape.water: Established vines need little irrigation; water young vines deeply and avoid wetting foliage.
grape.sunlight: Full sun; train and prune so the canopy stays open and dries quickly.
grape.soil: Well-drained soil, pH about 5.5-7.0; avoid waterlogging.
grape.temp_humidity: Prefers warm, dry growing seasons; humid, wet weather encourages black rot, mildews and other fungal diseases.
grape.nutrients: Excess nitrogen causes dense, disease-prone canopies; fertilise only after testing.
grape.pests: Watch for leafhoppers, mites, berry moths and birds.

orange.water: Deep watering when the top soil is dry; avoid both drought stress and soggy soil.
orange.soil: Well-drained soil, pH about 6.0-7.5; very sensitive to waterlogging.
orange.temp_humidity: Frost sensitive. Cold nights and heat stress both slow growth.
orange.nutrients: Citrus commonly shows zinc, iron or nitrogen deficiency, which can mimic disease. Test before feeding.
orange.pests: Watch for citrus psyllid (which can spread greening), leaf miner, scale and aphids. Report suspected citrus greening to local authorities.

peach.water: Deep watering during dry spells and fruit swell; avoid wetting foliage.
peach.sunlight: Full sun, with an open canopy through pruning.
peach.temp_humidity: Needs winter chill; blossoms are frost sensitive. Wet, warm weather favours bacterial and fungal disease.
peach.nutrients: Feed according to a soil or leaf test.
peach.pests: Watch for aphids, peach borers and plum curculio.

pepper.water: Even moisture; irregular watering can cause blossom-end problems. Water at the base.
pepper.soil: Rich, well-drained soil, pH about 6.0-6.8; mulch to hold moisture.
pepper.temp_humidity: Flowers drop in very hot (above about 32 °C) or cool (below about 15 °C) nights.
pepper.nutrients: Calcium-related blossom-end rot is usually an irregular watering problem; test before adding fertiliser.
pepper.pests: Watch for aphids, thrips, mites and pepper weevil.

potato.water: Even moisture, especially during tuber formation; avoid overhead watering late in the day.
potato.soil: Loose, well-drained, slightly acidic soil, pH about 5.0-6.5. Hill soil around stems to keep tubers covered.
potato.temp_humidity: Cool-season crop. Cool, wet, humid weather favours blight.
potato.nutrients: Moderate feeding; excess nitrogen gives leaf growth at the cost of tubers.
potato.pests: Watch for Colorado potato beetle, aphids and wireworms. Rotate crops (3-4 years) to cut disease carry-over.

raspberry.water: Steady moisture, about 25 mm per week; mulch to protect shallow roots.
raspberry.sunlight: Full sun; a little afternoon shade is fine in hot climates.
raspberry.soil: Well-drained soil rich in organic matter, pH about 5.5-6.5.
raspberry.temp_humidity: Cool to mild climates; good airflow reduces fungal problems.
raspberry.nutrients: Compost each year; test before applying fertiliser.
raspberry.pests: Watch for spider mites, cane borers and spotted-wing fruit flies.

soybean.water: Most important during flowering and pod fill; avoid waterlogging.
soybean.soil: Well-drained loam, pH about 6.0-7.0. Soybeans fix nitrogen with rhizobia bacteria, so nitrogen fertiliser is usually not needed.
soybean.temp_humidity: Warm-season crop; frost kills young plants.
soybean.nutrients: Check pH and phosphorus/potassium with a soil test.
soybean.pests: Watch for aphids, bean leaf beetles, stink bugs and spider mites.

squash.water: Deep watering at the base in the morning; wet foliage encourages disease.
squash.soil: Rich, well-drained soil, pH about 6.0-6.8; give plants space for airflow.
squash.temp_humidity: Warm-season crop, frost sensitive. Warm days and humid nights favour powdery mildew.
squash.nutrients: Compost-enriched soil; test before adding fertiliser.
squash.pests: Watch for squash bugs, vine borers and cucumber beetles.

strawberry.water: Shallow roots need regular moisture, about 25 mm per week; use drip or water at the base.
strawberry.soil: Well-drained, organic-rich soil, pH about 5.5-6.5; mulch with straw.
strawberry.temp_humidity: Cool, moist weather suits growth; crowded, humid beds encourage fungal disease.
strawberry.nutrients: Light feeding; test first. Replace beds every 3-4 years.
strawberry.pests: Watch for slugs, spider mites, aphids and birds.

tomato.water: Deep, even watering at the base, about 25 mm per week; irregular watering causes cracking and blossom-end rot.
tomato.soil: Rich, well-drained soil, pH about 6.0-6.8; mulch, stake and prune for airflow.
tomato.temp_humidity: Fruit set suffers above about 32 °C or below about 10 °C at night. Warm, humid, wet weather favours blights and leaf mould.
tomato.nutrients: Heavy feeder, but yellowing lower leaves can also come from disease or watering; test before fertilising.
tomato.pests: Watch for whiteflies (which spread leaf-curl virus), spider mites, aphids and hornworms.

brown_spots: Fungal or bacterial leaf spot diseases
browning_edges: Some diseases such as leaf scorch
powdery_coating: Powdery mildew, favoured by humid nights, dry days and poor airflow
curling: Sap-feeding insects such as aphids, mites or whiteflies

_preventive: Buy healthy, certified seed or plants and rotate crops each season.
Water at the base in the morning so foliage dries quickly.
Space and prune plants for airflow; remove weeds and fallen debris.
Inspect leaf tops and undersides weekly and photograph changes.
Clean tools between plants and quarantine new plants for a couple of weeks.
Use mulch and compost to buffer moisture and improve soil health.
_escalate: Symptoms spread quickly across many plants or into new areas.
You suspect a regulated disease (e.g. citrus greening) or a viral disease.
Valuable crops, orchards or food-safety decisions are involved.
You are considering a pesticide or fungicide, which should follow a confirmed diagnosis and local rules.
The result is inconclusive and the plant keeps declining.
